threshold_description: 'Children' means people under fifteen. NOTE: the Section One principle protects under-EIGHTEENS, but every operative rule using the word 'children' means under 15.
exceptions_conditions: Affects application of Rules 1.3, 1.10, 1.13, 1.27. Conflating the two ages mis-applies those rules.
ambiguity_note: Recorded explicitly because it is a known conflation trap (C-05).
verbatim_quote: Children are people under the age of fifteen years

threshold_description: 'Appropriate scheduling' is judged on: nature of content; likely number and age range of child viewers (taking into account school time, weekends and holidays); programme start and finish time; nature of the channel/programme; likely audience expectations for that channel at that time and day.
exceptions_conditions: Broadcasters serving ECTT Parties must also consider time differences in the country of reception.
verbatim_quote: protected by appropriate scheduling from material that is unsuitable

threshold_description: Binding definition of 'context' (8 factors): editorial content; the service; TIME OF BROADCAST; what is scheduled before and after; degree of harm/offence likely; likely size and composition of audience and audience expectation; extent to which content can be signalled in advance; effect on those coming across it unawares.
exceptions_conditions: This is the mechanism by which the SAME content is compliant at one hour and a breach at another with no rating change. Section One must be read with Section Two.
ambiguity_note: Central to the whole UK design: time of broadcast is a formal component of context.
verbatim_quote: Context includes (but is not limited to):

threshold_description: Material that might SERIOUSLY impair the physical, mental or moral development of people under eighteen.
exceptions_conditions: None. No contextual justification, no technical measure and no scheduling cures this.
ambiguity_note: Hard pre-check: should be enforced in code, not left to prompt reasoning.
verbatim_quote: might seriously impair the physical, mental or moral development

threshold_description: Broadcasters must take all reasonable steps to protect people under eighteen.
exceptions_conditions: Open-ended duty; informs every other decision.
verbatim_quote: must take all reasonable steps to protect people under eighteen

threshold_description: Children must be protected by appropriate scheduling from material unsuitable for them.
time_restriction_text: Determined by the appropriate-scheduling factors, not a fixed clock time.
exceptions_conditions: Does NOT apply to BBC ODPS. This is the rule most often cited in enforcement (see UK-P1 precedent).
verbatim_quote: Children must...be protected by appropriate scheduling from material that is unsuitable for them...

threshold_description: Television broadcasters must observe the watershed. Material unsuitable for children should not, in general, be shown before 21:00 or after 05:30.
exceptions_conditions: Does NOT apply to BBC ODPS. Displaced by 20:00 for unprotected premium subscription film services (UK-SCH-003) and disapplied where mandatory daytime protection is in place (UK-FLM-003).
ambiguity_note: The single most important UK bright line. Note it is an OPEN-ENDED period, structurally unlike the French closed windows.
verbatim_quote: should not, in general, be shown before 2100 or after 0530

threshold_description: Premium subscription film services WITHOUT protection operate a 20:00 watershed rather than 21:00.
exceptions_conditions: Conditional on service type AND absence of protection. Requires service_type input. inherits_time=05:30 from UK-SCH-002: the source gives these services a 2000 watershed and is silent on when it ends, because the end is the general 0530.
ambiguity_note: Proves the watershed itself is service-dependent, not universal.
verbatim_quote: not protected as set out in Rule 1.24 the watershed is at 2000

threshold_description: The transition to more adult material must not be unduly abrupt at the watershed. The strongest material should appear later in the schedule.
exceptions_conditions: A programme starting after 21:00 should not open with its strongest material; a programme crossing 21:00 must not suddenly become unsuitable.
ambiguity_note: No numeric threshold exists. Escalate to human review when a test case places strong material in the first minutes after 21:00.
verbatim_quote: It should not commence with the strongest material

threshold_description: Clear information about content that may distress some children should be given, if appropriate, taking into account the context.
exceptions_conditions: 'If appropriate' - discretionary, context-driven.
verbatim_quote: For television programmes broadcast before the watershed

threshold_description: Drugs, smoking, solvents and alcohol must not be featured in programmes made primarily for children without strong editorial justification; and must not be condoned, encouraged or glamorised in other programmes before the watershed without editorial justification.
exceptions_conditions: Two different thresholds: 'strong editorial justification' for children's programmes vs 'editorial justification' elsewhere pre-watershed.
ambiguity_note: The two-tier justification standard is easy to flatten; keep both.
verbatim_quote: must not be featured in programmes made primarily for children

threshold_description: Violence, its after-effects and descriptions of violence (verbal or physical) must be appropriately limited in programmes broadcast before the watershed, and must be justified by the context.
time_restriction_text: Restriction bites before 21:00; post-watershed governed by context.
exceptions_conditions: 'Appropriately limited' AND 'justified by the context' - a double test. Context per UK-DEF-003.
ambiguity_note: Primary violence rule. No intensity scale is given in the Code; applied thresholds come only from enforcement precedent.
verbatim_quote: must be appropriately limited in programmes broadcast before the watershed

threshold_description: Programmes made primarily for children must not include material that condones or glamorises violent, dangerous or seriously antisocial behaviour likely to encourage imitation.
time_restriction_text: Applies at all times to children's programmes.
exceptions_conditions: Turns on programme type, not clock time.
verbatim_quote: easily imitable by children in a manner that is harmful or dangerous

threshold_description: Dangerous behaviour, or behaviour easily imitable by children in a manner that is harmful, must not be featured before the watershed unless there is editorial justification.
exceptions_conditions: Cross-refers to Rules 2.4 and 2.5.
verbatim_quote: Dangerous behaviour, or the portrayal of dangerous behaviour

threshold_description: THE MOST OFFENSIVE LANGUAGE must not be broadcast before the watershed.
time_restriction_text: Prohibited before 21:00. No contextual justification available pre-watershed.
exceptions_conditions: Absolute pre-watershed. Post-watershed use still subject to Rule 2.3 context.
ambiguity_note: Note: 'the most offensive language' is a defined Ofcom concept informed by its periodic audience-attitudes research; the Code itself does not enumerate the words.
verbatim_quote: The most offensive language must not be broadcast before the watershed

threshold_description: Offensive language must not be broadcast in programmes made for younger children.
time_restriction_text: Applies at all times to programmes for younger children.
exceptions_conditions: Turns on programme type, not clock time.
verbatim_quote: Offensive language must not be used in programmes made for younger children

threshold_description: Offensive language must not be broadcast before the watershed unless justified by the context. In any event, FREQUENT USE of such language must be avoided before the watershed.
exceptions_conditions: The frequency limb is independent of the context limb ('in any event').
ambiguity_note: Requires CUMULATIVE counting, not presence/absence. Extraction stage must record counts with timecodes.
verbatim_quote: frequent use of such language must be avoided before the watershed

threshold_description: Material equivalent to the BBFC R18 rating must not be broadcast at any time.
exceptions_conditions: None. Survives every access/technical measure including MDP.
ambiguity_note: Hard pre-check in code.
verbatim_quote: Material equivalent to the...R18-rating must not be broadcast at any time.

threshold_description: 'Adult sex material' (strong sexual images/language broadcast for the primary purpose of sexual arousal) may only be broadcast between 22:00 and 05:30, on premium subscription or pay-per-view/night services operating with MANDATORY RESTRICTED ACCESS.
time_restriction_text: 22:00-05:30 only, and only on eligible services with mandatory restricted access.
exceptions_conditions: NOT unlocked by mandatory daytime protection - MDP expressly excludes adult sex material.
ambiguity_note: Three distinct UK access concepts must not be conflated: mandatory restricted access (this rule), mandatory daytime protection (films), and no protection. A model treating 'PIN protected' as one concept will wrongly allow this in daytime.
verbatim_quote: broadcast for the primary purpose of sexual arousal or stimulation

threshold_description: Material broadcast after the watershed containing strong or explicit sexual images/language, but which is NOT 'adult sex material', must be justified by the context.
exceptions_conditions: Boundary with Rule 1.18 turns on 'primary purpose of sexual arousal'.
ambiguity_note: Escalate because the 1.18/1.19 boundary carries a large consequence: if material is 'adult sex material' it is confined to 22:00-05:30 behind mandatory restricted access, whereas under 1.19 it is merely context-justified post-watershed. The test turns on 'primary purpose', which is an editorial judgment, not a content feature.
verbatim_quote: images and/or language of a strong or explicit sexual nature

threshold_description: Representations of sexual intercourse must not occur before the watershed unless there is a SERIOUS EDUCATIONAL PURPOSE. Any discussion or portrayal of sexual behaviour before the watershed must be editorially justified and appropriately limited.
exceptions_conditions: 'Serious educational purpose' is a higher bar than ordinary editorial justification.
verbatim_quote: Representations of sexual intercourse must not occur before the watershed

threshold_description: Nudity before the watershed must be justified by the context.
exceptions_conditions: Nudity is NOT automatically post-watershed; context can justify it earlier.
ambiguity_note: Common over-rating trap: treating any nudity as automatically post-watershed.
verbatim_quote: Nudity before the watershed

threshold_description: No film REFUSED classification by the BBFC may be broadcast, unless it has subsequently been classified or the BBFC has confirmed it would not be subject to compulsory cuts under current standards. Restrictions also apply to cut versions.
time_restriction_text: No permitted time unless subsequently classified/confirmed.
exceptions_conditions: Survives MDP - unchanged by the 2018 review.
ambiguity_note: Hard pre-check in code.
verbatim_quote: No film refused classification by the British Board of Film Classification

threshold_description: BBFC 18-rated films (or their equivalent) must not be broadcast before 21:00 on ANY service, except where there is mandatory daytime protection in place.
exceptions_conditions: Amended with effect 1 Jan 2019: the previous pay-per-view-specific carve-out was replaced by the general MDP concept.
ambiguity_note: THE clearest proof that rating does not determine hours: the same BBFC 18 film is barred pre-21:00 on one service and permitted at any hour on another, purely because of a technical access measure.
verbatim_quote: must not be broadcast before 2100, on any service

threshold_description: Where MANDATORY DAYTIME PROTECTION is in place, programmes unsuitable for children that would usually be scheduled post-watershed, and films up to BBFC 18 or equivalent, may be broadcast AT ANY TIME OF DAY. Clear information must be provided about the content and about the protection in place.
exceptions_conditions: MDP = a PIN protection system in place pre-2100 and post-0530, non-removable by the user, required on each entry, with accurate metadata. Excludes adult sex material. Does not cure R18 or refused-classification films. WHICH SERVICES MAY USE MDP IS NOT ESTABLISHED HERE: an earlier version of this row asserted it is unavailable to free-to-air DTT and to channels off a vertically integrated pay-TV platform. That wording appears in NO stored source. It came from the Ofcom MDP statement, which was never retrieved (only its landing page). Removed rather than kept at high confidence; tracked as C-17. Treat eligibility as an open question for a UK reviewer.
ambiguity_note: service_type AND access_control are mandatory inputs. If absent, the correct output is a missing-information flag, NOT an assumption of free-to-air.
verbatim_quote: PIN protection system in place pre-2100 and post-0530

threshold_description: Films up to BBFC 15 or equivalent may be broadcast from 20:00 on premium subscription film services WITHOUT mandatory daytime protection.
exceptions_conditions: Carve-out retained in the 2018 review: Ofcom had proposed removing it and did not.
verbatim_quote: pre-2000 and post 0530 for up to BBFC 15-rated films

threshold_description: Pay-per-view services may broadcast films up to BBFC 18 or equivalent at any time, provided mandatory daytime protection is in place. They must additionally provide content information, operate a detailed itemised billing system, and make subscribers aware of their child-protection systems.
exceptions_conditions: Billing and subscriber-information duties are additional and are not per-asset checkable.
verbatim_quote: Pay per view services may broadcast up to BBFC 18-rated films

threshold_description: BBFC R18-rated films must not be broadcast.
exceptions_conditions: None. Unchanged by the 2018 MDP review.
ambiguity_note: Hard pre-check in code.
verbatim_quote: BBFC R18-rated films must not be broadcast

threshold_description: Demonstrations of exorcism, occult practices or paranormal activity PRESENTED AS REAL must not be shown before the watershed. Programmes treating such activity as entertainment must not be broadcast when significant numbers of children may be expected to be watching. DRAMA, FILM AND COMEDY ARE EXEMPT.
time_restriction_text: Not before 21:00 where presented as real.
exceptions_conditions: Three-way split: presented-as-real (pre-watershed ban), entertainment (audience-based restriction), fiction (exempt).
ambiguity_note: The fiction exemption is a frequent over-rating trap.
verbatim_quote: Demonstrations of exorcisms, occult practices and the paranormal

threshold_description: Material which contains HATE SPEECH must not be included in television services except where it is justified by the context.
time_restriction_text: No clock time of its own. The context test imports the time of broadcast as one of its eight factors, so the hour is an input to the judgment but never determines it.
exceptions_conditions: Hate speech is defined expansively (intolerance on grounds of disability, ethnicity, social origin, gender, sex, gender reassignment, nationality, race, religion or belief, sexual orientation, colour, genetic features, language, political or any other opinion, membership of a national minority, property, birth or age). Distinct from Rule 3.1, which is an ABSOLUTE prohibition on incitement with no context escape.
ambiguity_note: Weigh against Article 10 freedom of expression; Ofcom decisions here turn on editorial framing (debate, drama, news) more than on the hour. Never resolve this automatically: a later hour does not cure hate speech, it is only one factor among eight. Escalate every hit to a UK compliance reviewer.
verbatim_quote: spread, incite, promote or justify hatred

threshold_description: Material which contains ABUSIVE OR DEROGATORY TREATMENT of individuals, groups, religions or communities must not be included in television services except where it is justified by the context.
time_restriction_text: No clock time of its own. Same context route as Rule 3.2.
exceptions_conditions: Lower threshold than Rule 3.2: abuse or derogatory treatment need not reach hate speech. Cross-refers to Rule 4.2 (Religion). Catches comedy and satire aimed at a community, which is the common false-negative for an automated classifier.
ambiguity_note: The most likely rule in the whole table to be missed by a content-description pipeline, because the trigger is TREATMENT rather than depicted subject matter: a description listing no violence, sex or drugs can still breach this. Escalate to a UK compliance reviewer.
verbatim_quote: abusive or derogatory treatment of individuals

threshold_description: DEFINITION. 'Mandatory restricted access' means a PIN-protected system, or other equivalent protection, which CANNOT BE REMOVED BY THE USER and which restricts access solely to those authorised to view.
time_restriction_text: Not a time rule. This is the definition the any-hour permissions are conditional on.
exceptions_conditions: The operative words are 'cannot be removed by the user'. A service-level parental control the viewer can switch off is NOT mandatory restricted access, so a title relying on it for an any-hour permission is in breach. Distinct from 'mandatory daytime protection', the pre-2100/post-0530 variant - the two are not interchangeable.
verbatim_quote: which cannot be removed by the user

threshold_description: IMPLEMENTATION. Restricted access must be provided AS THE DEFAULT. A service may not satisfy the requirement by offering a PIN the viewer has to set up; the gate must be on before the viewer arrives.
time_restriction_text: Not a time rule. Determines whether the any-hour permission is validly engaged.
exceptions_conditions: The most commonly misread requirement in the access-control set, because an opt-in PIN looks like compliance and is not. Guidance rather than Code text, hence rank 3, but it states how Ofcom reads a binding rule.
verbatim_quote: as the default, rather than requiring PIN setting by the viewer

threshold_description: CONDITIONS PRECEDENT to the any-hour permission, from the CURRENT Code text. Clear information must be provided with the content to help adults assess its suitability for children, AND the mandatory daytime protection in place must be CLEARLY EXPLAINED TO ALL VIEWERS. A gate nobody has been told about does not satisfy the rule.
time_restriction_text: Not a time rule itself, but the any-hour permission does not exist unless satisfied.
exceptions_conditions: These read as housekeeping and are not - they are conditions on the permission. The UK's nearest analogue to the French signaletique, discharged by INFORMATION rather than a pictogram, so a pipeline looking for a French-style on-screen symbol will report the UK as having no equivalent, which is wrong.
ambiguity_note: The sufficiency of the information is a judgment; its ABSENCE is not. Treat a missing information commitment as a bright-line fail and the adequacy of wording as a review item.
verbatim_quote: must be clearly explained to all viewers

threshold_description: Trailers are caught by the under-eighteens scheduling rules in their own right. A trailer does NOT inherit the permission of the programme it advertises.
time_restriction_text: The trailer is assessed against the slot it occupies, not the slot of its feature.
exceptions_conditions: The practical trap: a compliant post-watershed film generates a trailer that runs in a daytime break and breaches, with no change to the trailer's content. A pipeline that reasons only about the feature asset cannot see this.
verbatim_quote: both programmes and trailers are subject to this rule

threshold_description: THE WATERSHED DOES NOT APPLY AT ALL to a channel while mandatory daytime protection is in place. This is a disapplication, not a relaxation: the time question is removed rather than adjusted.
time_restriction_text: No window. The watershed ceases to bind while MDP is in place.
exceptions_conditions: Read with Rules 1.24 and 1.25. This is the concrete mechanism behind AVMSD art. 6a offering scheduling OR technical measures as ALTERNATIVES, and the reason this system reports three axes rather than two: an access control can remove the hours question entirely. Ranked 1 so it defeats the general watershed rule (UK-SCH-002) on conflict.
ambiguity_note: Verify the MDP is genuinely non-removable before applying this. The disapplication is only as good as the gate: if the protection fails UK-ACC-001's 'cannot be removed by the user' test, the watershed snaps back and the title is in breach from the first frame.
verbatim_quote: does not apply to channels when mandatory daytime protection

threshold_description: LOCKING SPECIFICATION for category V. The personal code must be AT LEAST FOUR DIGITS, must NOT be 0000, must NOT be visible on screen, and must be used EXCLUSIVELY for this purpose. The subscriber MUST NOT be able to deactivate the lock. It must re-arm on every change of broadcast context - channel change, standby, decoder shutdown, decoder or card change - activate for each new category V programme, and stay synchronised for its whole duration.
time_restriction_text: Not a time rule. These are the conditions the 00:00-05:00 permission depends on.
exceptions_conditions: The French analogue of the UK 'cannot be removed by the user' test, but far more prescriptive. A service meeting the UK standard does NOT automatically meet this one: the exclusivity requirement - the code may not double as a general parental PIN - and the re-arm-on-context-change requirement have no UK equivalent.
ambiguity_note: Engineering compliance, not editorial. Verify with the platform operator rather than the scheduling team: a broadcaster may not know whether its distributor's decoder satisfies criteria (e) or (f).
verbatim_quote: must include at least four digits (except 0000)

threshold_description: COMPLIANCE DEADLINES HAVE ALL ELAPSED: criteria (a)-(d) by 1 Jan 2005, (f) by 1 Jan 2006, (e) by 1 Jan 2008, and the transitional regime ended 1 Jan 2008. The scheme is fully in force with NO transitional relief available. Publishers and distributors must also report to the regulator ANNUALLY on implementation.
exceptions_conditions: Recorded because those elapsed dates were the specific reason this instrument's currency was doubted. Elapsed means FULLY IN FORCE, not expired - the opposite of the worry. An old instrument whose deadlines have all passed is the strongest kind of current law.
clause_ref: notice of 15 Dec 2004, II.B.2 and III.B
verbatim_quote: a report on the implementation of the measures taken

threshold_description: TRANSITION. Material scheduled to start before but continue past 21:00 must not ABRUPTLY become unsuitable, and content commencing after the watershed must observe a SMOOTH TRANSITION to more adult material. It must not open with the strongest content it holds.
time_restriction_text: Applies across the 21:00 and 05:30 boundaries rather than at a single instant.
exceptions_conditions: The watershed is a ramp, not a gate. A film cleared for 21:00 that opens on its most violent scene breaches this even though every clock-time check passes. REGULATOR EXAMPLES: Hell's Kitchen USA (ITV2) and Amores Perros (TCM) were both decided on this point. Viewers can be concerned at strong adult material immediately after the watershed when a significant number of children could still be watching.
ambiguity_note: Needs the running order, not just the start time - information a content description usually does not carry. Flag whenever a post-watershed asset's first scene is among its strongest.
verbatim_quote: It should not commence with the strongest material

threshold_description: TIMESHIFT (+1) SERVICES. Where the same content is broadcast an hour later on a +1 service, the later transmission must itself be suitable for the audience it will then reach. Broadcasters may need to schedule EARLIER on the main service so the +1 transmission still concludes before children return from school.
time_restriction_text: Effective hours differ between a service and its +1 by one hour, in both directions.
exceptions_conditions: The same file is compliant on one service and in breach on the other, with no editorial change whatsoever. A pipeline keyed to 'the asset' cannot represent this; it must reason per transmission. Note the risk runs the counter-intuitive way too: content placed while children are at school lands an hour later, when they are home.
ambiguity_note: Requires knowing whether a +1 service exists for the channel and whether the asset is carried on it. Rarely present in a content description - ask.
verbatim_quote: the same content is broadcast an hour later

threshold_description: TRAILERS ARE UNANNOUNCED. Because trailers are not signposted in advance, viewers meet them unawares, so a trailer for post-watershed content shown pre-watershed must contain ONLY pre-watershed-appropriate material. Trailers restricted away from children's programmes should also be kept away from sport and family entertainment, which attract significant child audiences.
time_restriction_text: Judged in its own slot, never inheriting the advertised programme's permission.
exceptions_conditions: This supplies the REASON behind the inheritance rule and extends it: the restriction is not only around children's programming but around anything drawing a child audience, which includes live sport - a slot nobody thinks of as a child-protection risk. REGULATOR EXAMPLES: Candy Bar Girls (Channel 5) and the Stylista trailer (Channel Five).
ambiguity_note: A trailer carrying images that would warrant a warning before the full programme is unlikely to be acceptable pre-watershed at all.
verbatim_quote: so they come across them unawares

threshold_description: MASKING IS NOT AUTOMATIC COMPLIANCE. Where masked ('bleeped') offensive language is frequent, the cumulative effect on viewers can be similar to that of the unedited language. Frequent use may require more rigorous editing, or may mean the programme is not appropriate pre-watershed at all.
time_restriction_text: Does not create its own window; governs whether a pre-watershed edit works.
exceptions_conditions: The common and expensive mistake: assume a post-watershed programme can be made daytime-safe by bleeping. Frequency is the trigger, not the presence of masking, so an edit can be technically thorough and still fail. Some content cannot be edited down to pre-watershed at all because of adult THEMES rather than specific words.
ambiguity_note: Requires a count and distribution of instances, which a content description rarely gives. Escalate any pre-watershed broadcast of material originally made for after it.
clause_ref: Post-watershed content edited for pre-watershed transmission
verbatim_quote: cumulative effect on viewers similar to that of

threshold_description: AUDIENCE COMPOSITION BEFORE 21:00 IS NOT UNIFORM. The watershed matters most for children aged 5 to 8, and trust in pre-watershed programming is essential particularly in the approach to 19:30. Programmes starting before the watershed and ending after it may hold special appeal for children, ESPECIALLY DURING SCHOOL HOLIDAYS.
time_restriction_text: The nearer to 19:30, the stronger the expectation - a gradient, not a flat pre-21:00 band.
exceptions_conditions: Contradicts the intuition that 20:55 is nearly post-watershed and therefore nearly free. And school holidays change the audience without changing the clock, so the same slot on the same channel carries a different risk in August.
ambiguity_note: Transmission DATE is needed, not only the time. A content description that gives a slot but no date cannot settle this.
verbatim_quote: especially during school holidays

threshold_description: EASILY IMITABLE METHODS. Hanging, or preparations for hanging, must be treated with particular care if easily imitable, above all before the watershed, unless the setting gives strong grounds for believing imitation is unlikely.
time_restriction_text: Pre-watershed is the aggravating factor; the concern does not vanish after 21:00.
exceptions_conditions: The operative test is IMITABILITY plus SETTING, not the presence of the act. A period drama and a contemporary bedroom scene are judged differently on identical events, which is why RUN 1 records `treatment` as a separate field from what happens.
ambiguity_note: Overlaps with the suicide and self-harm rules and must never be auto-decided. Escalate to a UK compliance reviewer in every case.
verbatim_quote: if easily imitable

threshold_description: AUDIENCE SIZE AND BROADCASTER SIZE. A larger audience, such as on a mainstream channel with popular appeal, raises the contextual justification required. A small broadcaster is NOT thereby permitted to transmit potentially harmful material without adequate protection: the obligation applies to all programmes regardless of reach.
time_restriction_text: Not a time rule. Expands the time-of-broadcast factor in the context definition.
exceptions_conditions: Resolves a real asymmetry: audience size can make a decision STRICTER but never looser. Expect the reverse argument from a niche channel; it is not available.
ambiguity_note: The channel's typical audience size and profile is required, and is almost never in a content description. REVIEW FLAG DELIBERATELY 'no': see below.
clause_ref: Guidance Notes Section 2, meaning of context
verbatim_quote: The timing of a broadcast may affect the composition of its audience

threshold_description: WARNINGS MUST BE ADEQUATE, NOT MERELY PRESENT. The effectiveness of a warning depends on its frequency and its positioning within the programme. For a longer programme a single message at the beginning may not be sufficient.
time_restriction_text: Not a time rule. Governs whether an information-based mitigation actually works.
exceptions_conditions: Matters because a warning is one of the main ways a broadcaster earns a slot it would not otherwise get. A pipeline that records 'warning: yes' as a boolean cannot represent this, and will credit an inadequate warning with mitigation it has not earned.
ambiguity_note: Needs the warning's wording, placement and repetition - not just that one exists. Treat a bare 'warning given' claim as unverified.
verbatim_quote: a single message at the beginning

threshold_description: A BBFC CERTIFICATE DOES NOT SET THE SLOT. The legacy ITC code scheduled films by strict reference to their BBFC rating; the Ofcom Code has in the main DISPENSED with that link. Films are scheduled like any other content, appropriately for the audience. A recent BBFC classification is a useful INDICATION of suitability, not a determinant.
time_restriction_text: No window of its own. Governs how much weight a certificate carries in the hours decision.
exceptions_conditions: The single most important row for anyone building on this table, because it is the regulator stating the rating/hours separation directly rather than me inferring it. CALIBRATION the guidance supplies: since 'children' means people under fifteen and material unsuitable for children should not generally be shown before 2100, it is UNLIKELY that a recently BBFC 15-rated film could be scheduled during the day. That is a usable threshold for a judgment rule - a presumption against, not a prohibition.
ambiguity_note: Treat a BBFC certificate as evidence feeding the scheduling judgment, never as the answer. Reporting a certificate as though it were a broadcast decision is a category error this rule exists to prevent.
verbatim_quote: dispensed with these rules relating scheduling to ratings

threshold_description: DECIDED CASE. A BBFC 15 action film containing frequent graphic violence - mass shootings, a beheading with the severed head then carried on screen, a man choked to death - broadcast at 11:30 BREACHED Rule 1.3. Ofcom weighed the BBFC 15 certificate as indicating unsuitability for under-15s, the absence of any warning or signposting, and the repeated depictions of killing as unsuitable for daytime viewing.
time_restriction_text: 11:30 is far pre-watershed; the finding does not fix a permissible hour, only that this one was not.
exceptions_conditions: The table's only hard calibration point for violence. Useful as an ANCHOR, not a threshold: it says this combination at this hour breached, not where the line sits. Note what did NOT save the broadcaster - an apology, an internal investigation, the explanation that a newly appointed scheduler made an unintentional error, and refresher training already completed. Mitigation after transmission does not undo a breach, which is the whole argument for catching it beforehand.
ambiguity_note: One case is not a calibration set. Treat as the single datum it is, and collect more before relying on interpolation between it and anything else.
verbatim_quote: well before the watershed without any warning or signposting

threshold_description: CONTEXT CAN JUSTIFY THE CONTENT AND STILL NOT JUSTIFY THE SLOT. In Toofan, Ofcom opened under both the scheduling rule and the offence rule, then DROPPED the offence limb - the violence was sufficiently contextualised within the film - while still finding a SCHEDULING breach on the same broadcast.
time_restriction_text: Not a time rule. Governs how the offence and scheduling determinations relate.
exceptions_conditions: The strongest available authority for this system's three-axis design, and it comes from a decided case rather than from inference. Editorial context defended the material as material; it did nothing for the hour. So a pipeline that resolves 'is this justified by the context?' once, and reuses the answer for both questions, will reach the wrong result in exactly this shape of case - and this shape is common, because a competent film almost always contextualises its own violence.
ambiguity_note: Run the offence and scheduling determinations separately and report both. Never let a finding of editorial justification discharge the scheduling question.
clause_ref: Bulletin issue 553, footnote 2 and Rule 1.3 decision
verbatim_quote: sufficiently contextualised within the film

threshold_description: THE CULTURAL AND RELIGIOUS CALENDAR AFFECTS AUDIENCE COMPOSITION. Ofcom weighed that the broadcast fell during the three-day Eid-ul-Adha celebrations, when many Muslim families and communities gather together, as increasing the likelihood that children were in the audience.
time_restriction_text: Does not move the watershed. Raises the expected child audience within existing hours.
exceptions_conditions: Nothing in the Code text says this; it emerges only from a decided case. It generalises badly and that is the point - the relevant festivals depend on the channel's community, so a system scaled across countries CANNOT infer them from a single calendar. Pairs with the school-holidays factor: both change who is watching without changing the clock or the content.
ambiguity_note: Needs the transmission DATE and knowledge of the channel's audience. A date alone is not enough without knowing which communities the service serves - ask a local expert rather than deriving it from a public-holiday table.
verbatim_quote: increasing the likelihood that children could have been watching

threshold_description: WARNINGS SHOULD CONVEY SEVERITY, NOT ONLY PRESENCE. Ofcom's research found audiences expect content warnings to indicate not only that violence is present but how severe it is, using terms such as 'graphic' or 'explicit'. Audiences also expect graphic and realistic violence to be post-watershed and rely on warnings to manage viewing.
time_restriction_text: Not a time rule. Determines whether a warning earns the mitigation claimed for it.
exceptions_conditions: Makes a boolean 'warning: yes' field inadequate. A warning saying 'contains violence' before content audiences would describe as graphic does not meet the expectation this describes, so it should not be credited as mitigation.
ambiguity_note: Capture the warning's actual wording. Treat an unquoted claim that a warning was given as unverified.
clause_ref: Bulletin issue 553, audience research cited in the decision
verbatim_quote: not only the presence of violence but also its severity

threshold_description: Religious programmes containing claims that a LIVING PERSON (or group) has SPECIAL POWERS OR ABILITIES must treat such claims with due objectivity AND must not broadcast such claims when significant numbers of children may be expected to be watching.
time_restriction_text: No clock time. Restriction is keyed to the likely child audience, not the watershed.
exceptions_conditions: Double test, like Rule 2.5: due objectivity AND the audience restriction. Section Four otherwise concerns religious content standards and is out of scope.
ambiguity_note: THIS RULE SITS OUTSIDE SECTION ONE and was missing from v1. Found by reviewing sections 3-10 for relevance. It is the close cousin of Rule 1.27 (occult/paranormal as entertainment), which uses the same 'significant numbers of children' test rather than the watershed - so a solution that only reads Section One misses a genuine child-audience broadcast restriction. Note the test is AUDIENCE-based, not time-based: there is no hour that automatically satisfies it.
verbatim_quote: special powers or abilities

threshold_description: Due care must be taken over the physical and emotional welfare and the dignity of under-18s who take part in or are otherwise involved in programmes, IRRESPECTIVE OF ANY CONSENT given by the participant or a parent/guardian. Under-18s must not be caused unnecessary distress or anxiety.
exceptions_conditions: Consent is expressly irrelevant.
ambiguity_note: Relevant where a content description involves minors as participants; not a scheduling rule.
verbatim_quote: Due care must be taken over the welfare and the dignity

threshold_description: Material which may cause offence must be justified by the context. Such material may include offensive language, violence, sex, sexual violence, humiliation, distress, violation of human dignity, and discriminatory treatment or language.
exceptions_conditions: Supplies the harm categories the UK actually recognises - useful as the UK category vocabulary.
verbatim_quote: material which may cause offence is justified by the context

threshold_description: Programmes must not include material (whether in individual programmes OR IN PROGRAMMES TAKEN TOGETHER) which, taking into account the context, condones or glamorises violent, dangerous or seriously antisocial behaviour and is likely to encourage others to copy such behaviour.
exceptions_conditions: 'In programmes taken together' makes cumulative, cross-programme assessment explicit.
ambiguity_note: Cross-programme accumulation cannot be assessed from a single asset description - flag for channel-level review.
verbatim_quote: condones or glamorises violent, dangerous or seriously antisocial

threshold_description: METHODS of suicide and self-harm must not be included in programmes except where they are editorially justified AND ALSO justified by the context.
exceptions_conditions: DOUBLE test - both limbs required. A single-condition check under-rates.
ambiguity_note: Always escalate. Two reasons: the double test ('editorially justified' AND 'justified by the context') is easy to collapse into one, and the downside of an under-rating here is imitative harm rather than mere offence. No automated verdict should stand alone on suicide or self-harm method depiction.
verbatim_quote: must not be included in programmes except where they are editorially justified

threshold_description: Pre-watershed music videos: sexualised images not banned but must be editorially justified and appropriately limited; explicit sexual behaviour avoided; intrusive or prolonged shots of body parts increase sexual impact; BDSM imagery not prohibited but explicit imagery avoided (shot length, repetition and overall theme considered); provocative/sexualised dancing limited; lyrics clearly focused on sex avoided.
exceptions_conditions: NICHE MUSIC CHANNELS STILL CARRY RESPONSIBILITY toward possible child viewers - a small or genre-specific audience does not remove the duty. Whether the video was supplied as a child-audience edit (e.g. marked 'pre 9pm') is a relevant input.
ambiguity_note: Lyrics that seem mild on audio alone can become highly sexualised when paired with sexual imagery - so audio and video must be assessed TOGETHER, not independently. Independent tagging systematically under-rates music videos.
verbatim_quote: the sexualised clothing and dance routines of performers

threshold_description: Pre-watershed music videos should not show performers inadequately covered, particularly the breasts, genitals or buttocks. Underwear and bikinis are not prohibited; whether the clothing is PRESENTED SEXUALLY is what matters.
exceptions_conditions: Fetish clothing combined with sexual behaviour needs particular care.
verbatim_quote: the sexualised clothing and dance routines of performers

threshold_description: In music videos, violence should be limited and justified by context, and not explicit, gratuitous or easily imitable. Images of suicide are not banned but must be very carefully limited so that no details could prompt imitation.
exceptions_conditions: Images of suicide are not banned outright, which makes this a calibration question rather than a yes/no one.
ambiguity_note: Escalate. 'Very carefully limited so that no details could prompt imitation' is a threshold about DETAIL, not about presence, so it cannot be decided from a content tag alone - it needs the actual shot description. Same imitative-harm downside as UK-SUI-001.
verbatim_quote: bondage, dominance and sadomasochism in music videos

threshold_description: Trailers shown before the watershed for post-watershed programmes must contain only material appropriate for pre-watershed broadcast. Viewers do not choose to watch trailers. Trailers may need restricting around children's programming, family shows and sports coverage.
time_restriction_text: Pre-watershed trailers held to pre-watershed standard.
exceptions_conditions: The parent programme's own permitted slot does NOT license its trailer.
verbatim_quote: include only content that is appropriate for a pre-watershed audience

threshold_description: Specific care areas: family viewing shows (suit family viewing throughout; extra caution if running past 21:00; daytime repeats need separate thought); soaps (each episode scheduled on its own merits - a long-running storyline does not itself supply context); post-watershed content edited for daytime (some content remains unsuitable regardless of editing; FREQUENT BLEEPING HAS A CUMULATIVE EFFECT).
exceptions_conditions: +1 (timeshift) services need specific attention: a 21:00 broadcast becomes 22:00 on +1, but a 20:00 broadcast becomes 21:00.
ambiguity_note: The +1 point is a good adversarial test case - it changes the answer with no change to content.
verbatim_quote: family viewing programmes

threshold_description: The scheduling requirements in Rules 1.3, 1.4, 1.5 and 1.6 DO NOT APPLY to BBC on-demand programme services.
exceptions_conditions: For BBC ODPS, 'context' excludes scheduling/time of broadcast and instead covers the manner of access, including measures to prevent children viewing.
ambiguity_note: Out of scope for linear TV but recorded so the scope boundary is explicit and testable.
verbatim_quote: Scheduling requirements in Rules 1.3, 1.4, 1.5 and 1.6 do not apply to BBC ODPS.

threshold_description: Ofcom has a statutory duty to set standards ensuring 'that persons under the age of eighteen are protected'. This is the legal basis for Section One of the Broadcasting Code.
exceptions_conditions: Also s.3(4)(h). The AVMS Regulations 2020 (SI 2020/1062) implemented the revised AVMSD duties; content standards for broadcast TV remain in the Ofcom Code.
ambiguity_note: Never cite as the operative rule for a decision - it sets the duty, not the threshold.
verbatim_quote: that persons under the age of eighteen are protected

threshold_description: No programme liable to SERIOUSLY harm (nuire gravement) the physical, mental or moral development of minors may be made available by a radio or television service.
exceptions_conditions: None. Tier 1 of the French two-tier harm standard - no time or technical measure cures it.
ambiguity_note: The French analogue of Ofcom Rule 1.1. Hard pre-check in code.
verbatim_quote: nuire gravement

threshold_description: Programmes liable to HARM (nuire) the physical, mental or moral development of minors must not be made available UNLESS it is ensured - by the CHOICE OF BROADCAST TIME and by ANY APPROPRIATE TECHNICAL PROCESS - that minors are not normally liable to see or hear them.
time_restriction_text: Determined by the instrument chosen (time and/or technical measure).
exceptions_conditions: Tier 2 of the two-tier standard. Mirrors AVMSD art. 6a(1). This is the statutory hook for the entire French time-restriction system AND for the category V locking regime.
ambiguity_note: The two-tier structure (seriously harm vs harm) must be represented or absolute bans get treated as schedulable.
verbatim_quote: nuire à l'épanouissement physique, mental ou moral des mineurs

threshold_description: Between 06:00 and 22:00, and a fortiori in programmes intended for young audiences, violence - INCLUDING PSYCHOLOGICAL VIOLENCE - must not be able to be perceived as continuous, as the only solution to conflicts, or in an exacerbated form.
exceptions_conditions: CATEGORY-INDEPENDENT: a programme can be category I or II and still breach this. Replaced by delib. 2014-17.
ambiguity_note: A solution that only reasons about the I-V categories will miss this rule entirely.
verbatim_quote: la violence, meme psychologique

threshold_description: Programmes on HISTORICAL OR CONTROVERSIAL subjects may be broadcast before 22:00 if the editor provides EDUCATIONAL SUPPORT going beyond a mere written or spoken warning.
time_restriction_text: Permits pre-22:00 broadcast subject to the condition.
exceptions_conditions: A warning alone is expressly insufficient.
verbatim_quote: un accompagnement pédagogique visant à contextualiser les scènes

threshold_description: For difficult images or testimony concerning particularly dramatic events, in news and other programmes, the editor must take precautions and WARN THE PUBLIC IN ADVANCE.
exceptions_conditions: Applies to news, which France otherwise exempts from classification.
verbatim_quote: images difficilement soutenables ou des témoignages

threshold_description: Category I - programmes for all audiences. NO pictogram.
exceptions_conditions: The editor classifies via an internal commission de visionnage.
verbatim_quote: categorie I (aucune signaletique) : les programmes pour tous publics

threshold_description: Category II (-10) - programmes CERTAIN SCENES of which are liable to shock minors under 10.
verbatim_quote: certaines scènes susceptibles de heurter les mineurs de 10 ans

threshold_description: Category III (-12) - cinematographic works BANNED TO UNDER-12s IN CINEMAS, and programmes liable to DISTURB under-12s, in particular where THE PROGRAMME resorts in a REPEATED way to physical or psychological violence.
exceptions_conditions: A cinema -12 interdiction pulls a film into at least this category. Per CSA practice a film carrying a CNC 'avertissement' is classified -12 for TV.
ambiguity_note: 'Repeated' is a frequency/pattern test, not a severity test - requires counting across the asset. IMPORTANT: delib. 2014-17 replaced the fifth alinea of art. 2 and BROADENED this definition twice over - 'leur scenario recourt de facon repetee ET SYSTEMATIQUE' became 'le programme recourt de facon repetee'. So (a) repetition alone now suffices, systematic use is no longer required, and (b) the test is the programme as a whole, not just its scenario. An extraction working from the pre-2014 wording UNDER-RATES. The superseded pre-2014 wording is recorded in the C-09 conflict entry rather than as a rule row, since the manifest now carries only current materials. Verified 2026-11-06 against the STORED French primary text (FR-R1c/FR-R1d), which reads '...notamment lorsque le programme recourt de facon repetee a la violence physique ou psychologique'. C-10 RESOLVED by the same check: the words 'sexualite adulte' do NOT occur anywhere in the binding recommendation, so the 'ou evoque la sexualite adulte' limb on Arcom's public page (FR-S1c) is a PRACTICE GLOSS, not binding text. Do not treat adult sexuality as an independent -12 trigger; the binding trigger is repeated violence. Arcom may still apply the gloss in practice, so flag borderline sexual-content cases for review rather than clearing them.
verbatim_quote: les programmes pouvant troubler les mineurs de 12 ans, notamment lorsque le programme recourt de facon repetee a la violence physique ou psychologique

threshold_description: The classification a film receives for CINEMA release MAY SERVE AS AN INDICATION for its television classification, but the editor must verify that the rating transfers without harm and MAY STRENGTHEN IT.
exceptions_conditions: French practice is explicitly to RAISE the age limit between cinema and television, because a child who could not enter the cinema can easily be in front of a TV set.
ambiguity_note: The CNC/cinema rating is an INPUT, never the output. The TV category is a separate determination and may be stricter.
verbatim_quote: peut servir d'indication pour leur classification

threshold_description: Reclassification procedure: works at least 20 YEARS since their last visa may be submitted for revision for TV broadcast, by JOINT request of editor and producer, at least 8 months before scheduling. Arcom forwards up to 20 requests per year to the Commission de classification, which must opine at least 1 month before broadcast.
exceptions_conditions: The only route by which the cinema classification commission revisits a rating for television purposes.
ambiguity_note: Procedural, not a per-asset rating rule. Recorded for completeness.
verbatim_quote: un délai d'au moins vingt ans s'est écoulé

threshold_description: Category II (-10): broadcast timing is left to the EDITOR'S DISCRETION, but such programmes MAY NOT BE PLACED WITHIN PROGRAMMES INTENDED FOR CHILDREN.
time_restriction_text: No clock restriction; placement restriction only.
exceptions_conditions: Particular care required for trailers scheduled near children's programmes.
ambiguity_note: Note there is NO time restriction for -10 - only a placement restriction. A model that assumes every age label implies an hour will invent one.
verbatim_quote: les horaires de diffusion de ces programmes sont laissés à l'appréciation

threshold_description: Category III (-12) on services OTHER THAN cinema channels and pay-per-view: must not be broadcast BEFORE 22:00.
exceptions_conditions: Subject to the exceptional derogation in FR-SCH-004. Cited against the CURRENT consolidated French text, not the 2005 JORF original: the hours happen to be unchanged since 2005, which is precisely why the amended art. 2 definition slipped past review (C-09).
ambiguity_note: C-02 RESOLVED 2026-11-06. The service mapping was originally taken from Arcom's garbled English machine translation. Now confirmed against the FRENCH text from two independent sources: Legifrance JORFTEXT000000446802 (the 2005 original) and the csa.fr consolidated page carrying the 'Modifiee par la deliberation n. 2014-17 du 5 mars 2014' banner. Both read identically: 'pour les chaines cinema et les services de paiement a la seance, ces programmes ne doivent pas etre diffuses le mercredi avant 20 h 30. Pour les autres services de television, ces programmes ne doivent pas etre diffuses avant 22 heures.' The Arcom French page for 2014-17 confirms art. 3 was replaced with the same wording.
verbatim_quote: Pour les autres services de television, ces programmes ne doivent pas etre diffuses avant 22 heures.

threshold_description: Category III (-12) on CINEMA CHANNELS and PAY-PER-VIEW services: must not be broadcast ON WEDNESDAYS BEFORE 20:30.
exceptions_conditions: A day-of-week-specific rule. Historically tied to the French school week.
ambiguity_note: C-02 RESOLVED 2026-11-06. The service mapping was originally taken from Arcom's garbled English machine translation. Now confirmed against the FRENCH text from two independent sources: Legifrance JORFTEXT000000446802 (the 2005 original) and the csa.fr consolidated page carrying the 'Modifiee par la deliberation n. 2014-17 du 5 mars 2014' banner. Both read identically: 'pour les chaines cinema et les services de paiement a la seance, ces programmes ne doivent pas etre diffuses le mercredi avant 20 h 30. Pour les autres services de television, ces programmes ne doivent pas etre diffuses avant 22 heures.' The Arcom French page for 2014-17 confirms art. 3 was replaced with the same wording.
verbatim_quote: pour les chaines cinema et les services de paiement a la seance, ces programmes ne doivent pas etre diffuses le mercredi avant 20 h 30.

threshold_description: Category III (-12) EXCEPTIONAL DEROGATION: may be broadcast AFTER 20:30, EXCEPT on Tuesdays, Fridays, Saturdays, the eve of public holidays, and during school holidays. Capped at 16 PROGRAMMES PER YEAR, of which at most 4 may be works banned to under-12s in cinemas. Remains subject to art. 1 para. 1.
time_restriction_text: After 20:30, with day and holiday exclusions.
exceptions_conditions: REQUIRES the broadcast DATE (not just time) and the French school-holiday calendar. The annual quota cannot be verified from a single asset description.
ambiguity_note: C-02 RESOLVED 2026-11-06. The service mapping was originally taken from Arcom's garbled English machine translation. Now confirmed against the FRENCH text from two independent sources: Legifrance JORFTEXT000000446802 (the 2005 original) and the csa.fr consolidated page carrying the 'Modifiee par la deliberation n. 2014-17 du 5 mars 2014' banner. Both read identically: 'pour les chaines cinema et les services de paiement a la seance, ces programmes ne doivent pas etre diffuses le mercredi avant 20 h 30. Pour les autres services de television, ces programmes ne doivent pas etre diffuses avant 22 heures.' The Arcom French page for 2014-17 confirms art. 3 was replaced with the same wording. QUOTA ALSO CONFIRMED in the French primary text (2026-11-06): 'Ces diffusions exceptionnelles ne peuvent exceder seize programmes par an, dont au maximum quatre oeuvres cinematographiques interdites en salles aux mineurs de 12 ans'. The earlier caveat that the 16/4 numbers rested only on the English rendering is withdrawn. Note the quotas remain channel-level facts: a per-asset prompt cannot verify them and must flag this for channel-level review.
verbatim_quote: Ces diffusions exceptionnelles ne peuvent exceder seize programmes par an, dont au maximum quatre oeuvres cinematographiques interdites en salles aux mineurs de 12 ans

threshold_description: Category IV (-16) on services OTHER THAN cinema channels and pay-per-view: reserved for a warned audience; may only be broadcast AFTER 22:30.
exceptions_conditions: No derogation equivalent to FR-SCH-004 is provided for category IV.
ambiguity_note: Corroborated by the Arcom public summary ('as of 10:30 pm'), the French government page, and multiple parliamentary answers - so this row is better evidenced than the cat. III rows.
verbatim_quote: reserves a un public averti, ces programmes sont diffusables seulement apres 20 h 30 sur les chaines cinema et les services de paiement a la seance et apres 22 h 30 sur les autres services de television

threshold_description: Category IV (-16) on CINEMA CHANNELS and PAY-PER-VIEW services: reserved for a warned audience; may be broadcast AFTER 20:30.
exceptions_conditions: Two hours earlier than on other services - a pure service-type effect with identical content.
ambiguity_note: Excellent demonstration that the age label alone does not determine the hour.
verbatim_quote: diffusables seulement apres 20 h 30 sur les chaines cinema et les services de paiement a la seance

threshold_description: Category V (-18): broadcast is governed ENTIRELY by Recommandation n. 2004-7 of 15 December 2004.
exceptions_conditions: art. 3 of FR-R1 delegates completely; the -18 hours are NOT stated in FR-R1.
ambiguity_note: A model asked for -18 hours must follow this pointer. Answering by analogy with -16 ('later than 22:30') is wrong.
verbatim_quote: soumise au respect de la recommandation n° 2004-7

threshold_description: Programmes which OFFEND HUMAN DIGNITY - in particular those depicting SEXUAL VIOLENCE, PERVERSIONS OR DEGRADATION - are banned from broadcast.
exceptions_conditions: None. No category, service type, hour or technical measure unlocks this.
ambiguity_note: Hard pre-check in code.
verbatim_quote: attentatoires à la dignité de la personne humaine

threshold_description: PORNOGRAPHIC programmes DEPICTING UNDER-18s are banned from broadcast.
exceptions_conditions: None.
ambiguity_note: Hard pre-check in code.
verbatim_quote: pornographique mettant en scène des personnes mineures

threshold_description: Programmes of EXTREME OR GRATUITOUS VIOLENCE are banned from broadcast.
exceptions_conditions: None. Distinguish from category V 'very great violence', which IS broadcastable within 00:00-05:00 on eligible services.
ambiguity_note: The boundary between 'very great violence' (cat. V, schedulable) and 'extreme or gratuitous violence' (banned) is a genuine judgment line and a likely source of disagreement. Flag near-threshold cases.
verbatim_quote: violence ou de violence gratuite

threshold_description: The PICTOGRAM must remain on screen FOR THE WHOLE DURATION of the programme (categories II-V under the 2014 text).
exceptions_conditions: Under the original 2005 text category II was 5 minutes at the start; 2012-57 and 2014-17 changed this.
ambiguity_note: Signage is a SEPARATE obligation from scheduling: a programme can be correctly scheduled and still breach by failing to display the pictogram. The C8 enforcement decision was precisely about signage.
verbatim_quote: présent à l'écran pendant toute la durée de la diffusion

threshold_description: A WRITTEN MENTION must also appear, either at the bottom of the screen in white for AT LEAST 1 MINUTE at the start, OR full-screen before the programme for AT LEAST 12 SECONDS. Wording: II 'deconseille aux moins de dix ans'; III 'aux moins de douze ans'; IV 'aux moins de seize ans'; V 'aux moins de dix-huit ans' (or the assigned cinema-ban wording).
exceptions_conditions: Decret n. 90-174 on prior public warnings continues to apply.
verbatim_quote: en bas d'écran, en blanc, au minimum pendant une minute

threshold_description: The classification must be made known to the public AT THE TIME OF BROADCAST, in TRAILERS, and in PROGRAMME SCHEDULES communicated to the press.
verbatim_quote: portée à la connaissance du public au moment de la diffusion

threshold_description: Trailers must display the PICTOGRAM OF THE PROGRAMME'S CATEGORY THROUGHOUT the trailer, and must NOT contain scenes likely to offend young viewers.
verbatim_quote: apparaît pendant toute la durée de la bande-annonce

threshold_description: Category III (-12) trailers MAY NOT AIR CLOSE TO CHILDREN'S PROGRAMMES. Category II trailers near children's programmes require particular care.
verbatim_quote: ne peuvent être diffusées à proximité des émissions pour enfants

threshold_description: Category IV (-16) trailers MAY NOT AIR BEFORE 20:30.
exceptions_conditions: Note the trailer time (20:30) differs from the programme time on non-cinema channels (22:30).
verbatim_quote: catégorie IV ne peuvent être diffusées avant 20 h 30

threshold_description: Music videos (videomusiques) are EXEMPT FROM SYSTEMATIC SIGNAGE.
exceptions_conditions: A deliberate special regime, not an oversight.
ambiguity_note: Contrast with the UK, which applies the ordinary watershed plus detailed content thresholds to music videos. The SAME music video can yield a hard UK verdict and a soft French one.
verbatim_quote: exonérées du caractère systématique de la signalétique

threshold_description: Music videos likely to offend young viewers SHOULD PREFERABLY be broadcast AFTER 22:00.
time_restriction_text: Soft preference for after 22:00 - NOT an absolute prohibition.
exceptions_conditions: The wording is a preference ('de preference'), not a prohibition. Do not output this as a hard limit.
ambiguity_note: A key precision test: a model that renders this as 'prohibited before 22:00' is OVER-rating and misstating the legal force of the rule. Worth an explicit test case.
verbatim_quote: l'éditeur s'attache à les diffuser après 22 heures

threshold_description: Programmes containing music videos whose THEMES ARE NOT AIMED AT CHILDREN OR TEENAGERS should nonetheless carry a WARNING.
verbatim_quote: selon des thématiques qui ne s'adressent ni aux enfants

threshold_description: Category IV (-16) - cinematographic works BANNED TO UNDER-16s IN CINEMAS, and programmes of an EROTIC character or of GREAT VIOLENCE, liable to harm the physical, mental or moral development of under-16s. Pictogram: a white circle carrying -16 in black.
time_restriction_text: See FR-SCH-005 (22:30 on general services), FR-SCH-006 (20:30 on cinema channels and pay-per-view) and FR-TRL-003 (20:30 for trailers).
exceptions_conditions: A cinema -16 interdiction pulls a work into at least this category. The erotic limb is distinct from the pornographic limb of category V and sits below it.
ambiguity_note: 'Grande violence' and 'tres grande violence' separate this category from V and the line between them is nowhere defined in the stored text. Both turn on degree, and the French scheme gives no worked examples, so a borderline work can be argued either way with a two-hour difference in the permitted slot on a general service.
verbatim_quote: programmes à caractère érotique ou de grande violence

threshold_description: Category V (-18) - cinematographic works BANNED TO UNDER-18s IN CINEMAS, and PORNOGRAPHIC programmes or programmes of VERY GREAT VIOLENCE, reserved for a warned adult audience and liable to harm the physical, mental or moral development of under-18s. Pictogram: a white circle carrying -18 in black.
time_restriction_text: Broadcast is governed entirely by recommandation 2004-7; see FR-CV-001 for the service eligibility gate and FR-CV-002 for the hours.
exceptions_conditions: Reaching this category does not by itself permit broadcast: FR-CV-001 gates WHICH services may carry it at all, and FR-CV-003 imposes a total prohibition on the rest.
ambiguity_note: The boundary with category IV turns on 'tres grande violence' against 'grande violence', and on 'pornographique' against 'erotique'. Neither pair is defined in the stored text. This boundary matters more than most: category IV is a late hour, category V is a total prohibition on any service not specially authorised.
verbatim_quote: programmes pornographiques ou de très grande violence

threshold_description: ELIGIBILITY GATE: only services with special access conditions may broadcast category V - 'cinema' channels, services with a high production-contribution commitment equivalent to cinema channels, or pay-per-view services - and only where access is limited so that under-18s cannot reach the content. Requests are EXAMINED INDIVIDUALLY by the regulator.
time_restriction_text: Eligibility precondition, not a time rule.
exceptions_conditions: On all other channels category V is TOTALLY PROHIBITED (see FR-CV-003).
ambiguity_note: VERIFIED against the primary text 2026-11-06. Quotes are from Arcom's own ENGLISH translation, which warns that only the original French is authentic - a French-qualified reviewer should re-check them against it.
verbatim_quote: subject to special access conditions

threshold_description: Category V (-18) programmes may be broadcast only BETWEEN 00:00 (MIDNIGHT) AND 05:00.
exceptions_conditions: Conditional on the FR-CV-001 eligibility gate being satisfied first, plus locking (FR-CV-004) and signage.
ambiguity_note: Source text dates from 2004 with compliance deadlines of 2005/2006/2008 all elapsed; CSA->Arcom (2022) and the 2021 AVMSD transposition decree both postdate it. Not confirmed still in force unamended. (C-03) Corroborated by the Arcom public summary page ('between midnight and 5 a.m.'), which raises confidence in the figure even though the source text's currency is unconfirmed.
verbatim_quote: can only be shown between midnight and 5am

threshold_description: On services that are NOT eligible under FR-CV-001, category V programmes are subject to a TOTAL PROHIBITION ON BROADCAST.
time_restriction_text: No permitted time on non-eligible services.
exceptions_conditions: None.
ambiguity_note: SECONDARY-SOURCED INFERENCE. The proof quote comes from a government summary page, not the primary instrument. The primary says only that the regulator 'only authorizes' eligible services; a total ban elsewhere follows reasonably from that but remains an INFERENCE. A French regulatory lawyer should confirm it before this row is used to refuse a broadcast.
verbatim_quote: Sauf sur les chaines autorisees, ces programmes font l'objet d'une interdiction totale de diffusion.

threshold_description: DIGITAL LOCKING: category V must be locked at the DECODER level requiring a personal code, with an on-screen lock message. The lock must reactivate when the broadcast context changes and stay synchronised with the programme. The code must be at least FOUR DIGITS, not 0000, hidden when entered, used only for this purpose, and IMPOSSIBLE FOR SUBSCRIBERS TO DISABLE.
exceptions_conditions: Analogue services: from 1 Jan 2006 received WITHOUT access unless the subscriber opts in in writing.
ambiguity_note: VERIFIED against the primary text 2026-11-06. Quotes are from Arcom's own ENGLISH translation, which warns that only the original French is authentic - a French-qualified reviewer should re-check them against it.
verbatim_quote: This program is locked because it is harmful to persons under 18

threshold_description: QUANTITY LIMITS: the regulator caps the number of category V broadcasts in each service's CONVENTION. Separately, if a non-pay-per-view bundle includes services showing MORE THAN 208 category V programmes per year (about 4 per week), the offer must also be available WITHOUT those services, on terms that do not favour the bundle.
exceptions_conditions: A channel/distributor-level obligation.
ambiguity_note: Not answerable from a single asset description. Must not be attempted by a per-asset prompt. Source text dates from 2004 with compliance deadlines of 2005/2006/2008 all elapsed; CSA->Arcom (2022) and the 2021 AVMSD transposition decree both postdate it. Not confirmed still in force unamended. (C-03)
verbatim_quote: more than 208 category V programs per year

threshold_description: MARKETING CONDITIONS: category V content may not be included in promotional offers aimed at people without a qualifying subscription; pay-per-view category V may only be sold INDIVIDUALLY; opt-in offers may not be priced more favourably than versions without category V content.
exceptions_conditions: Distributor-level.
ambiguity_note: Recorded for completeness only. Source text dates from 2004 with compliance deadlines of 2005/2006/2008 all elapsed; CSA->Arcom (2022) and the 2021 AVMSD transposition decree both postdate it. Not confirmed still in force unamended. (C-03)

threshold_description: Broadcasts of category V must display the -18 rating AND a WARNING about harm to minors and the legal sanctions under ARTICLE 227-22 of the French Penal Code. Distributors/publishers must regularly remind subscribers how the lock works; contracts must include this information; annual implementation reports go to the regulator.
exceptions_conditions: The penal-code warning is specific to category V.
ambiguity_note: VERIFIED against the primary text 2026-11-06. Quotes are from Arcom's own ENGLISH translation, which warns that only the original French is authentic - a French-qualified reviewer should re-check them against it.

threshold_description: CHANNEL CONVENTIONS: every conventionnee channel signs an individual convention with Arcom containing its own protection-of-minors articles, which CAN BE STRICTER than the general recommendation. Enforcement cites the convention alongside the recommendation (e.g. the C8 decision cites convention arts. 2-3-7, 2-4, 4-2-1 with reco. 2005-5 arts. 2 and 4).
time_restriction_text: Channel-specific; may tighten any rule above.
exceptions_conditions: Parliamentary material notes conventions have LOWERED the category III limit to 22:00 'or less, with permanent signage' for particular channels.
ambiguity_note: PROMOTED from draft 2026-11-07. What is now PROVEN from a stored source (FR-V1): a convention is an individual binding agreement between the regulator and the channel, breach of it is a manquement in its own right, and the regulator derives its enforcement power from the convention alongside the statute. What remains UNCOLLECTED is the CONTENT of any individual convention, so this row tells a decision that an extra layer of binding obligation exists for a French channel and that it must be checked, not what it says. C-06 stays open for that. | There is no consolidated document containing all applicable French rules for a given broadcast: the set is statute + reco. 2005-5 as amended + (for -18) reco. 2004-7 + THAT CHANNEL'S convention. For Task 2 this is a per-licensee data source that cannot be scraped generically and needs a local expert.
verbatim_quote: aux stipulations précitées de l'article 2-3-7 de sa convention

threshold_description: Member States must ensure that audiovisual media services which MAY IMPAIR the physical, mental or moral development of minors are only made available in such a way that MINORS WILL NOT NORMALLY HEAR OR SEE THEM. Measures may include selecting the TIME OF BROADCAST, AGE VERIFICATION TOOLS, or OTHER TECHNICAL MEASURES, and must be PROPORTIONATE to the potential harm. The most harmful content, such as gratuitous violence and pornography, is subject to the strictest measures.
time_restriction_text: Not itself a time rule - mandates an outcome and permits alternative means.
exceptions_conditions: NOT directly applicable to a broadcast; binds Member States, who implement nationally. UK retained equivalent duties via SI 2020/1062.
ambiguity_note: ROOT CAUSE of the 'rating does not equal hours' problem: the directive mandates the outcome and lists time, age verification and other technical measures as ALTERNATIVES. Two Member States can lawfully reach the same outcome with completely different instruments - France chose graded descriptors plus fixed hours; the UK chose a single watershed plus contextual judgement plus PIN. Never cite as the operative rule for a decision.
verbatim_quote: The most harmful content, such as gratuitous violence and pornography, shall be subject to the strictest measures.

threshold_description: Member States must ensure providers give viewers SUFFICIENT INFORMATION about content which may impair minors' development, using A SYSTEM DESCRIBING THE POTENTIALLY HARMFUL NATURE of the content. Co-regulation is encouraged.
exceptions_conditions: Separate from and additional to the access/time measures in art. 6a(1).
ambiguity_note: Independent corroboration for carrying a fixed content_category dimension separate from the age level: the regulators themselves concluded an age number alone is insufficient. EU notification material for the French 2021 decree states content indicators/descriptors (violence, sex, distress, etc.) were needed because the existing programme symbol gave no indication of the TYPE of harmful content.
verbatim_quote: provide sufficient information to viewers about content

threshold_description: Personal data of minors collected or generated pursuant to art. 6a(1) must not be processed for commercial purposes such as direct marketing, profiling or behaviourally targeted advertising.
ambiguity_note: Not a content or scheduling rule. Recorded so the scope boundary is explicit.
verbatim_quote: shall not be processed for commercial purposes
